Small blocks: %1$s reads and %2$s writes a second
What the marks on a card mean

Class 10, U1 and V10: writes at least 10 MB/s. U3 and V30: at least 30 MB/s. A1: at least 1500 small reads and 500 small writes a second, which helps games made of many files. A2 promises more, but this console uses A2 cards like A1 cards.
A real size check is paused on this card. Continue it or delete its test data first.
Continue the check
Paused while writing, %1$s of %2$s. The test data stays on the card until you continue or delete it, so games may not be able to save until then.
Paused while reading back, %1$s of %2$s. The test data stays on the card until you continue or delete it, so games may not be able to save until then.
Delete the test data
Frees %1$s. The next check starts from the beginning.
Stop the check?
Pause keeps the test data on the card so you can continue later. Until then games may not be able to save. Stop deletes the test data.

This fills all the free space on %1$s for about %2$s, so games can\'t save there until it is done. Plug in the charger: the console stays awake. You can pause and continue later, or stop at any time. Your games and files are not touched.

%1$s of test data fills the card. Continue the check or delete the test data, so games can save again.
Internal storage
This card has no EASYROMS partition, so the tests use the internal storage on it. The real size check leaves 1 GB free for Android.
